title: Sinharaja endemic mornings
summary: Dawn walks after Sri Lanka's rainforest endemics, with a guide who knows the flock routes.
description: Sinharaja is the one place on the island where most of Sri Lanka's endemic birds can be found in a single forest. We walk the research trails at first light, when the mixed-species feeding flocks move through — often twenty or more birds crossing the path at once. Afternoons are for the quieter understorey species and for the rainforest's frogs, lizards and butterflies. Two nights lets you take two dawns; three makes the trip comfortable rather than rushed.

title: Highland birding at Horton Plains
location: Horton Plains & Nuwara Eliya, Central Highlands
summary: Cloud forest and montane grassland, for the endemics that live only at altitude.
description: Above 2,000 metres the forest changes completely, and so do the birds. We start early on the Horton Plains trails while the mist is still down, then work Victoria Park in Nuwara Eliya in the afternoon, which is small but reliably good for wintering migrants. Cold mornings — bring a layer, which surprises most people about the tropics.

title: Yala leopard tracking
summary: Full-day safaris in the park with the densest leopard population in the world.
description: Yala's block one holds leopards at a density found nowhere else, and a full day inside the park — rather than the usual half-day circuit — is what makes a sighting likely rather than lucky. Scrub jungle, lagoons and rock outcrops in the same drive, so the day gives you far more than the cats: elephant, sloth bear in the right season, and dry-zone birds around every water tank.

highlights.name: Sri Lankan leopard
highlights.note: Rock outcrops in the early morning

highlights.name: Sloth bear
highlights.note: Best odds when the palu fruits, June–July

title: Wilpattu and its villus
location: Wilpattu National Park, North Western Province
summary: The island's largest park, quieter than Yala, built around natural lakes.
description: Wilpattu is far bigger than Yala and sees a fraction of the vehicles, so the experience is slower and more solitary — you can sit at a villu, one of the park's natural sand-rimmed lakes, and simply wait for it to come to you. Leopard sightings take more patience here than at Yala, but the setting is the reward.

highlights.name: Sloth bear
highlights.note: Open scrub in the early morning

title: Ella hill trails
summary: Little Adam's Peak at sunrise, Ella Rock after breakfast, tea country in between.
description: Ella sits in a gap in the hills, which is why the walks here all end in a view. Little Adam's Peak is a gentle hour before breakfast; Ella Rock is a proper half-day on rougher ground. Between them are the Nine Arch Bridge, the Ravana waterfall and tea estates you walk straight through. Good for anyone who wants hill country without a multi-day trek.

title: Knuckles forest crossing
summary: Cloud forest, village paths and the ridgeline, on foot and away from the road.
description: The Knuckles range is the least visited of Sri Lanka's mountain landscapes: montane forest, terraced rice villages and a ridgeline that clears above the cloud by mid-morning. The route is walked between village guesthouses rather than hotels, which is the point of it — this is the part of the country that still runs at walking pace.

title: The ancient cities
summary: Two ancient capitals and the rock fortress between them, at the right hours.
description: Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa were the island's capitals for well over a thousand years between them, and Sigiriya's rock fortress sits on the road that links the two. The trick is timing: Sigiriya before the heat, Polonnaruwa by bicycle in the late afternoon, Anuradhapura around the rituals at the sacred bo tree rather than around the tour buses.

highlights.name: Sigiriya Lion Rock
highlights.note: Start at opening, before the heat

title: Kandy, temple and tea
summary: The Temple of the Tooth at evening puja, then the tea estates above the town.
description: Kandy is best taken slowly: the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic at the evening puja when the drummers start, a morning in the botanical gardens at Peradeniya, and an afternoon in a working tea factory on the hills above town where the whole process runs in front of you. If you travel in July or August, the Esala Perahera fills the streets for ten nights.

title: South coast and Galle Fort
summary: Quiet days on the south coast, with the Dutch fort at Galle an afternoon away.
description: The south coast is where a journey tends to end: a few unhurried days at Mirissa, and one afternoon walking the ramparts of Galle Fort, which is best entered late in the day when the walls hold the light and the streets inside cool down. Blue whales pass offshore between December and April for anyone who wants one more early start.

title: Rainforest photography days
summary: Built around the light, not the checklist — hides, slow mornings, long lenses.
description: A photography-paced trip: we stay put where the light is good instead of covering ground. Early mornings at the forest edge for mixed flocks, the middle of the day for macro work on frogs, lizards and leaf litter, and late afternoon for the canopy from above at Kithulgala. Vehicle and walking pace are set by what you are shooting, and Nandana has guided wildlife photographers since 2002.

title: Kithulgala river days
summary: White-water rafting, canyoning and a zip line, on the edge of the rainforest.
description: The Kelani river at Kithulgala runs grade 2–3 through rainforest, which makes it the island's adventure base: rafting in the morning, canyoning at the waterfalls in the afternoon, and a zip line across the valley for anyone still standing. All of it runs with licensed local operators we work with, and the same forest is full of birds if you want a quiet second day.
